feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong senior digital/public-sector CV with clear domain positioning, credible progression, and solid evidence of scope. It reads professionally, but impact is diluted by repetition, limited quantified outcomes beyond scale metrics, and a few style/grammar inconsistencies.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: progression at NACo is credible and supports the “Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader” positioning well.  
- Strong relevance and scope: Drupal modernization, analytics stack, governance, multimedia, and AI search align tightly with senior digital platform roles.  
- Good use of scale indicators: 10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers, and team/channel ownership add credibility.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidate to create a tighter, more scannable structure.  
- Add sharper outcomes: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than results. Include measurable impact such as engagement growth, efficiency gains, adoption, cost savings, or campaign performance.  
- Fix writing/style consistency: “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; “Ranked among the top public universities…” is weak/irrelevant filler; capitalization is inconsistent (“Coleman DAVIS” vs standard title case); punctuation/bullet formatting in project and experience sections is uneven. No major misspellings found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible positioning with clear public-sector relevance, but it overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and recent experience bullets. Tightening it around distinctive value and scale will make it sharper.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace “building the platforms” with stronger leadership language like “leading” or “modernizing” to sound more senior.
- Add scale or scope from recent roles where possible, e.g., enterprise web estates, large publisher groups, or high-traffic environments.
- Trim the long list of functions; emphasize 3–4 core strengths most relevant to target roles.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience leading enterprise web modernization, governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Builds scalable digital ecosystems spanning analytics, editorial systems, multimedia, and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “editorial systems” repeat language already covered in Core Competencies.
- The subtitle already signals leadership; avoid repeating “digital leader” elsewhere if space is tight.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block largely repeats the header and Topline Skills. It would be more effective if tightened, made more parallel in style, and focused on differentiating strategic strengths rather than restating adjacent sections.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use shorter, more scannable noun phrases with consistent structure; avoid mixing “operations,” “systems,” and “experiences” unevenly.
- Prioritize the strongest, most distinctive areas first: enterprise web modernization, governance/editorial systems, analytics, AI-enabled search, and workflow automation.
- Consider sharpening public-sector relevance: “Public-sector advocacy communications” is more specific than “Advocacy and public-sector communications.”
- Possible rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial systems • Analytics, reporting, and optimization • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Multi-channel communications leadership • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Repeats several phrases from the header, especially “enterprise web modernization,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “AI-enabled user experiences.”
- Overlaps heavily with Topline Skills; consider making this section broader and more executive-level, leaving tools/details elsewhere.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and overlaps with work-experience bullets. Tightening phrasing and emphasizing outcomes or scope will make it more distinctive as a footer highlight section.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Use consistent action/result structure: “Built/Developed [project] using [methods/features] to [outcome].”
- Tighten wording: change “designed for continued campaign growth” to “built for future campaign expansion”; spell out “10-by-20-foot” for style consistency.
- If possible, add one concrete outcome, audience, or scale detail to 1–2 projects.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, and advocacy video series substantially repeat current freelance and NACo experience bullets.
- “Editorial storytelling,” “web features,” and “production and distribution” are somewhat generic; sharpen to avoid repeating broader skills already covered elsewhere.

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and project footer. Tighten it around 4–5 high-impact contributions and add outcomes, scale, or scope wherever possible.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper lead: “Serve as strategic communications consultant to a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvement, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Combine overlapping bullets on systems/workflows/governance: “Built cross-channel workflows, governance standards, and analytics processes to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Make the Drupal/campaign work outcome-led: “Designed and launched Drupal-based campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits.” Add usage, launch count, or stakeholder reach if available.
- Tighten technical/AI bullets: “Delivered CMS/front-end enhancements for high-traffic public sites and led an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content, and discovery UX.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “AI-enabled search” and the microsite example already appear in Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level unless you add distinct results.
- Governance/analytics language repeats the summary and NACo role; emphasize what is new in this engagement.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget, leading platform modernization and operational scale.”
- Rewrite bullets to emphasize outcomes:
- “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio, increasing capacity for advocacy programming, event production, and recurring multimedia content.”
- “Implemented analytics stack across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery, improving leadership reporting and decision-making.”
- “Established digital governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning systems to improve consistency and execution.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; either add stronger results or cut it.
- Governance/editorial workflow language also appears elsewhere; keep this version at the enterprise/leadership level.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry is too close to the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more clearly about execution leadership, channel ownership, and systems built before promotion.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and progression: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging ahead of promotion to Director of Digital Media.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct contributions: “Owned production and distribution of four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet outcome-led: “Launched and grew a weekly advocacy video update into a recurring policy communications channel distributed across web, email and social.”
- Combine workflow/editorial bullets: “Built stronger cross-team editorial planning and more consistent digital publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Helping scale” and “helped improve” sound soft; use direct ownership verbs.
- Avoid repeating broad channel oversight already covered more strongly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline skills item overlaps heavily with the header, core competencies, and recent experience. It should be tighter, more distinctive, and framed around senior leadership strengths rather than generic capability labels.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive phrasing:  
- Enterprise digital strategy & transformation  
- Editorial governance & content operations  
- Cross-channel communications leadership  
- Public-sector stakeholder messaging  
- Audience strategy & content planning
- Consider swapping “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” for “Change management for complex publishing organizations” if targeting enterprise digital leadership roles.
- Keep each line noun-based and parallel; avoid broad terms like “leadership” and “planning” unless paired with a specific domain.
- If space allows elsewhere, reserve measurable proof points for experience bullets rather than this skills block.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” repeat language already used in the header and core competencies.
- “Advocacy messaging” is also reinforced in multiple NACo roles and recent projects.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize current, differentiating strengths tied to recent web modernization and AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters: “Drupal and CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Prioritize most relevant/recent items first: lead with Drupal, CMS modernization, integrations, and AI-enabled search; move older or less central platforms later or remove.
- Consider dropping one lower-signal platform here (for example SharePoint or Power Pages) unless it is important for target roles.
- If space allows, sharpen phrasing to outcomes-oriented language: “Enterprise CMS modernization” or “API-driven platform integrations” instead of generic nouns.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills higher-level and let Technical + IT hold the full platform list.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies and the header summary; mention it once here only if it remains a priority differentiator.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to capability-first, e.g. “Analytics strategy, dashboarding & optimization.”
- Tighten and group related items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity”
- Replace generic phrases with stronger business language: “KPI framework development” instead of “KPI design”; “executive reporting” instead of “leadership reporting”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy & dashboarding • KPI framework development • Executive reporting • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity • SEO and digital performance analysis”

- “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating that exact phrasing.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming

- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and older NACo experience. Tighten it to emphasize higher-level production capability and recent leadership-level event delivery rather than generic task skills.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, grouped phrasing: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ and multi-camera studio systems • Virtual event operations”

- “Studio operations” and “PTZ camera systems” may feel too tactical unless balanced with broader event-delivery language.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic keyword dump and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should either be tightened to emphasize strongest/recent platforms or reframed to show level of use.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize the most relevant, recent platforms first: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages**; move **GitHub Pages** to a lower-priority item or drop it if space is tight.
- If formatting allows, add proficiency/context instead of just names: **Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages**.
- Consider renaming the heading to **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner phrasing and consistency.
- If you want more impact, align with recent work: **Drupal-focused enterprise web platforms, plus WordPress, SharePoint and Power Pages**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; avoid listing the exact same platforms in both places without added context.
- “CMS modernization” already appears elsewhere, so don’t repeat that phrase here unless tied to a specific platform.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools that support recent Drupal, analytics, automation, and AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to something more specific, e.g. “Front-End & Technical Implementation.”
- Reorder by strongest/recent relevance: “JavaScript • HTML5/CSS3 • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions • jQuery”
- Consider adding brief qualifiers where true: “JavaScript (front-end enhancements), API integrations (CMS/workflow), GitHub Actions (deployment automation), Cloudflare Workers (edge scripting)”
- If space allows, replace older/generic terms with higher-value specifics tied to recent work, e.g. “structured search implementation” or “deployment automation”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” already appears in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the exact phrasing in both places.
- GTM overlaps somewhat with analytics/infrastructure themes elsewhere, so keep it only if you’ve used it hands-on.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already named elsewhere. Make it more purposeful by grouping tools by function and emphasizing systems/automation over basic collaboration apps.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Systems**
- Reorder by relevance/strength: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams**
- Consider adding light functional framing: **Automation & workflow design:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | **Project/work management:** Jira, Asana, Trello | **Team collaboration:** Slack, Microsoft Teams
- Drop weaker/older tools unless they are current differentiators; keeping 6–8 tools will feel sharper than a long list.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies/Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Basecamp may feel dated and lower-priority versus more recent enterprise tools already shown.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools for the candidate’s communications leadership profile, but this line is too bare and doesn’t reflect level of use or business context. It would be stronger if framed around campaign/email operations rather than just listing vendor names.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp** only if these were hands-on systems used recently; otherwise order by recency/relevance.
- If space allows, add light context: **Email marketing, member engagement and newsletter operations: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If one platform was primary in the NACo or consulting roles, place it first and consider dropping the least-used tool to keep the list credible and focused.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This overlaps with work-experience bullets about newsletters and digital channels; avoid adding outcome claims here unless they are not already covered there.
- “Engagement” is broad; don’t repeat analytics/automation concepts already covered in other Technical + IT categories.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” In the Technical + IT section, keep it tighter and more tool-focused; move methods like SEO/A/B testing/dashboarding into experience bullets if they drove results.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **GA4 • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console**
- If you want to keep one method term, use: **GA4 • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Microsoft Clarity • Search/UX optimization**
- Order by strongest/recent relevance: GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Clarity.
- If space allows elsewhere, quantify in recent roles instead: e.g., “Expanded analytics infrastructure across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery to improve reporting for a 10,000+ page site with 3.5M annual page views.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This line is nearly duplicated by **Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization**.
- “SEO,” “A/B testing,” and “Dashboarding” are capabilities, not tools; they fit better in Core Competencies or work experience.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but this reads broadly and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Tighten it to emphasize foundational impact, promotion, and any concrete outputs without repeating later leadership themes.

Suggested edit
- Lead with advancement and team-building: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team…”
- Make contributions more concrete: specify the website refresh scope, cadence of weekly video updates, number/type of livestreams, or audience/reach if known.
- Use sharper action verbs and trim filler: replace “supporting the creation of” / “strengthening workflows” with “helped launch” / “standardized.”
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team. Supported a major website refresh, standardized workflows across web, email, social and multimedia, produced recurring weekly video updates and livestreamed key events, and provided day-to-day oversight for a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this version focused on launching/establishing the format.
- “Strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations language; frame this as early process-building instead.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a notable “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Emphasize the launch and scope, and trim broad support language.

Suggested edit:
- Lead with the strongest differentiator: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “coordinated innovation and research projects” with clearer business support language: “Supported county innovation and policy initiatives through research coordination and program content development.”
- Tighten multimedia wording: “Produced digital and multimedia content for program and policy communications” instead of “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials.”
- If possible, add one concrete outcome: number of episodes launched, audiences served, programs supported, or types of deliverables produced.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid overemphasizing multimedia production here; later NACo roles already show stronger video/digital leadership.
- “Supporting organizational programs and policy work” is broad and may repeat later advocacy/editorial coordination language.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills list, but it reads a bit generic and overlaps with stronger multimedia claims already made in Core Competencies and recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize tools/software rather than broad capabilities.

Suggested edit:
- Rename/reshape as a pure tools line: “Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator”
